docs.title: FAQs
docs.text: FAQs FAQs Answers to the questions we hear most before a trip. How do I book a trip? Choose a trip, pick a date and send us a message. We confirm availability within two days and send a short form for each traveler. Can I cancel? Cancellations up to 30 days before departure are fully refunded. After that we keep a deposit of 20%, or move your booking to another date at no cost. What is included? Guides, local transport, technical gear and accommodation, unless the trip page says otherwise. Flights and travel insurance are not included. Do I need insurance? Travel insurance that covers outdoor activities is required for every trip. We can recommend providers in your country. How fit do I need to be? Each trip lists its difficulty. Easy trips suit anyone who walks or rides regularly; challenging ones need some training beforehand. Need more help? Give us a call at 1-800-800-0000. E-mail us at info@senda.example We love to talk adventures! Follow us Instagram Facebook X © 2026 Senda. docs.title: Climbing New Zealand
docs.text: Tall rock towers in the forest Turquoise lake between mountains Fjord seen from a ridge Climbing New Zealand Activity Rock Climbing Adventure type Overnight trip Trip length 7 days Group size 6 Difficulty Intermediate Price USD 2,400 Share this adventure Overview Seven days of guided rock climbing on the South Island, from sunny limestone crags to long alpine ridges with views over turquoise lakes. Every day ends at a lakeside lodge. Itinerary Two days of skills on single-pitch routes, three days of multi-pitch climbing, and a final alpine summit if the weather allows. What to bring Climbing shoes, a harness and layers for changing mountain weather. Ropes, helmets and hardware are provided. docs.title: Surfing the Cold North
docs.text: Surfing the Cold North Surfing the Cold North Thick wetsuits, empty line-ups and waves that roll in under the northern lights. We spent ten days chasing swell along a rocky Arctic coast, sleeping in fishermen's cabins and drying gear by wood stoves. Why go north Cold water means fewer crowds. A good 6 mm suit, boots and a hood make three-hour sessions possible even in midwinter, and the light at four in the afternoon is something you will not forget. Good to know When is the best season? From September to March, when autumn storms bring steady swell. Do I need to be an expert? An intermediate level is enough on the sheltered beaches. New trips every season. Learn how we travel. docs.title: Ski Touring Basics
docs.text: Ski Touring Basics Ski Touring Basics Skins on, heels free: ski touring trades the lift queue for a quiet climb and untracked snow. Here is what you need for your first season away from the resort. The gear Touring bindings, climbing skins and a pair of boots with a walk mode are the core. Add an avalanche transceiver, a shovel and a probe, and learn to use them before you need them. Start small Pick short, low-angle routes close to the resort, go with someone who has done it before, and check the avalanche bulletin every morning. New trips every season. Learn how we travel. docs.title: Camping in the Desert
docs.text: Camping in the Desert Camping in the Desert Days of silence, nights full of stars. Desert camping asks for careful planning, and pays it back with some of the clearest skies on the planet. Water first Plan for at least five liters per person per day, and cache water along the route when you can. Heat drops fast after sunset, so pack a warm layer. Leave no trace Desert soil takes decades to recover. Camp on durable ground, keep fires small or skip them, and carry everything out. New trips every season. Learn how we travel. docs.title: A City Skate Guide
docs.text: A City Skate Guide A City Skate Guide Smooth plazas, long downhill avenues and a community that meets every Sunday morning. We spent a weekend rolling across town with local skaters. Where to roll Start at the riverside promenade, then follow the old tram line uptown. Early mornings are quiet, and the security guards at the plazas are friendlier before ten. Join a session The Sunday group ride welcomes beginners. Bring a helmet, water and a few coins for coffee at the end. New trips every season. Learn how we travel.
